translations.literal: Empress Qinsheng, because of the nephew-and-uncle relationship, once visited his residence, performed rites at the shrine of the Empress Xianmu, and ordered attendants to support Duan Yuan so that he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Because of their nephew-and-uncle relationship, Empress Qinsheng once visited his residence, performed rites at the shrine of Empress Xianmu, and ordered attendants to support Duan Yuan so that he need not kneel and bow.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，卒，帝輟朝臨奠，賻典加等，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou he died; the Emperor suspended court to attend the funeral in person, enhanced the burial gifts, and posthumously appointed him Grand Master with the same ceremony as the Three Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanyou he died. The Emperor suspended court to attend his funeral in person, enhanced the burial gifts, and posthumously granted him grand master with ceremonial standing equal to the Three Councillors.

sentences.zh: 弟端愨，子評。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Duan Que; his son was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Duan Que; his son was Ping.

sentences.zh: 端愨字守道，官左藏庫使，執獻穆喪，辭起復，詔特給奉。

translations.literal: Duan Que, courtesy name Shoudao, held the post of Director of the Left Treasury; he observed mourning for Xianmu, declined recall to office, and an edict specially granted him salary.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Que, courtesy name Shoudao, held the post of director of the left treasury. He observed mourning for Empress Xianmu, declined recall to office, and an edict specially continued his salary.

sentences.zh: 累遷東上閣門使、幹辦三班院。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate and Superintendent of the Three-Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to commissioner of the eastern upper gate and superintendent of the Three-Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴群玉殿，仁宗獨賜珠花、飛白字，寵顧特異。

translations.literal: Once while attending a feast at the Hall of Collected Jade, Emperor Renzong alone bestowed pearl flowers and flying-white calligraphy on him, favoring him with exceptional regard.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending a feast at the Hall of Collected Jade, Emperor Renzong alone bestowed pearl flowers and flying-white calligraphy upon him, singling him out with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 知邢、冀、衛三州，至蔡州觀察使。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Xing, Ji, and Wei Prefectures, rising to Inspector of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Xing, Ji, and Wei Prefectures, rising to inspector of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，以安德軍留後卒，贈昭德軍節度使，諡曰恭敏。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou he died as Acting Military Governor of Andre Army, and was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Zhaode Army with the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he died while serving as acting military governor of Andre Army. He was posthumously made military governor of Zhaode Army and given the posthumous title Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 兄端懿，在嘉祐時嘗密請建儲，人無知者，卒於澶淵，端愨走護其喪以歸。

translations.literal: His elder brother Duan Yi, during the Jiayou period once secretly requested the establishment of an heir; no one knew of it. He died at Chanzhou and Duan Que rushed to escort his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Duan Yi had secretly petitioned for the establishment of an heir during the Jiayou period, a fact unknown to others. When Duan Yi died at Chanzhou, Duan Que rushed to escort his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 元豐間因進對，袖舊稿上之，神宗歎曰：「近世之賢戚也。」

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng period, when granted an audience, he drew old drafts from his sleeve and submitted them; Emperor Shenzong sighed and said: "A worthy kinsman of recent times."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng period, while granted an audience, he drew old drafts from his sleeve and submitted them. Emperor Shenzong sighed and said: "A worthy imperial kinsman of recent times."

sentences.zh: 由是端愨之名益著。

translations.literal: From this Duan Que's name became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this Duan Que's name became all the more renowned.

sentences.zh: 評字持正，由東頭供奉官八遷皇城使。

translations.literal: Ping, courtesy name Chizheng, from Eastern Head Palace Attendant was promoted eight times to Commissioner of the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, courtesy name Chizheng, rose eight ranks from eastern head palace attendant to commissioner of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 以父告老，授西上閣門使，為樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: Because his father requested retirement, he was appointed Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and served as Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his father requested retirement, he was appointed commissioner of the western upper gate and made chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出使陝西、河東，還，言鄜延之人皆謂城囉兀非便，乞速毀撤，解一路之患。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to Shaanxi and Hedong, upon his return he said the people of Fuyan all held that building the Luowu fortress was ill-advised, and requested its rapid demolition to remove the calamity of the entire circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as envoy to Shaanxi and Hedong, he reported that the people of Fuyan all believed building the Luowu fortress was ill-advised and pleaded for its rapid demolition to remove the danger facing the entire circuit.

sentences.zh: 師 出安南，調兵及河東，又言王師南征，而取卒於西北，使蠻聞之，得以窺我。

translations.literal: When the army marched to Annan and troops were drawn from Hedong, he again said that with the imperial army campaigning in the south while drawing soldiers from the northwest, if the barbarians heard this they could spy on our weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched against Annan and troops were drawn from Hedong, he again warned that with the imperial army campaigning in the south while drawing soldiers from the northwest, the southern peoples would hear of it and find an opportunity to probe our defenses.

sentences.zh: 所論事頗多，或見施行。

translations.literal: The matters he discussed were many, and some were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He raised many matters of policy, and some of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 然天資刻薄，招權不忌，多布耳目，采聽外事自效以為忠。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was harsh and mean, gathered power without scruple, widely placed informants, and gathered and listened to outside affairs to prove himself loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was harsh and calculating. He gathered power without scruple, widely planted informants, and monitored outside affairs to demonstrate his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 僥 幸進用，中外仄目。

translations.literal: Favored by fortune in his advancement, he was viewed with unease both within and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through favor rather than merit, and both inside and outside the court watched him with unease.

sentences.zh: 以榮州刺史出知潁州，還，幹當三班院。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Rong Prefecture he went out to serve as Prefect of Ying Prefecture; upon returning he managed the Three-Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Ying Prefecture from the post of prefect of Rong Prefecture. Upon returning he managed the Three-Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 副韓縝報聘契丹，且分畫河東地界，凡二年乃決。

translations.literal: As deputy to Han Zhen on a return mission to the Khitans, he also demarcated the boundaries of Hedong; it took two years to settle.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy to Han Zhen on a return mission to the Khitans, he also helped demarcate the Hedong boundary. The matter took two years to settle.

sentences.zh: 賜袍帶、金帛以賞勞。

translations.literal: Robes, belts, gold, and silk were bestowed as reward for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: Robes, belts, gold, and silk were bestowed to reward his service.

sentences.zh: 進成州團練使、知蔡州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regimental Commander of Cheng Prefecture and Prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regimental commander of Cheng Prefecture and appointed prefect of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈冀州觀察使，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Inspector of Ji Prefecture and granted one thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Ji Prefecture and granted one thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 評少涉書傳，嘗以公主遺奏召試學士院，改殿中丞，意不滿，辭之。

translations.literal: Ping in youth was versed in books and classics; once, because of a memorial left by the princess, he was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy and was changed to Palace Court Assistant; dissatisfied, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Ping had some exposure to books and classics. Once, on the strength of a memorial left by the princess, he was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy and promoted to palace court assistant, but he was dissatisfied and declined.

sentences.zh: 後二年再召試，復止遷一官，愈不悅，至上書辨論。

translations.literal: Two years later he was again summoned for examination, but again received only a single rank promotion; even more displeased, he submitted a memorial arguing his case.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was summoned for examination again, but was promoted only one rank once more. Still more displeased, he submitted a memorial arguing his case.

sentences.zh: 及卒，人無憐者。

translations.literal: When he died, no one pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, no one mourned him.

sentences.zh: 曹佾字公伯，韓王彬之孫，慈聖光獻皇后弟也。

translations.literal: Cao Yi, courtesy name Gongbo, was the grandson of Prince of Han Wang Bin and the younger brother of Empress Cisheng Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi, courtesy name Gongbo, was the grandson of Prince Han Wang Bin and the younger brother of Empress Cisheng Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 性和易，美儀度，通音律，善奕射，喜為詩。

translations.literal: His nature was easygoing, his appearance handsome, he was versed in music, skilled at archery and chess, and fond of composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was easygoing and bore himself with graceful dignity. He was versed in music, skilled at archery and chess, and fond of composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 自右班殿直累進殿前都虞候、安化軍留後。

translations.literal: From Right Watch Commander he was successively promoted to Chief Inspector of the Palace Command and Acting Military Governor of Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: From right watch commander he was successively promoted to chief inspector of the Palace Command and acting military governor of Anhua Army.

sentences.zh: 言者謂年未四十毋典軍， 出知澶、青、許三州，徙河陽。

translations.literal: Critics said he was not yet forty and should not command armies; he went out to serve as Prefect of Cao, Qing, and Xu Prefectures, then was transferred to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that he was not yet forty and should not command armies. He was sent out as prefect of Cao, Qing, and Xu Prefectures, then transferred to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 以建武軍節度使為宣徽北院使，知鄆州，改保靜、保平軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、景靈宮使，加兼侍中，封濟陽郡王。

translations.literal: As Military Governor of Jianwu Army he became Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, Prefect of Yan Prefecture; he was changed to Military Governor of Baojing and Baoping Armies, Concurrent Secretariat Director, and Director of Jingling Palace, additionally appointed Concurrent Secretariat Director, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As military governor of Jianwu Army he became commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat and prefect of Yan Prefecture. He was then made military governor of Baojing and Baoping Armies, granted the title of concurrent Secretariat director, appointed director of Jingling Palace, further appointed concurrent Secretariat director, and enfeoffed as duke of Jiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 神宗每谘訪以政，然退朝終日，語不及公事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong often consulted him on policy, yet after court he spent the whole day without speaking of official business.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong often consulted him on policy, yet after leaving court he would spend the entire day without discussing official business.

sentences.zh: 帝謂大臣曰：「曹王雖用近親貴，而端拱寡過，善自保，真純臣也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the chief ministers: "Prince Cao, though elevated by near kinship, sits upright with few faults, knows how to protect himself well — a truly pure minister!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the chief ministers: "Though Prince Cao rose through near imperial kinship, he sits upright with few faults and knows how to protect himself — a truly loyal and upright minister!"

sentences.zh: 進對未嘗名。

translations.literal: When he advanced for audience he was never addressed by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When he came forward for audience he was never addressed by personal name.

sentences.zh: 元豐中以疾告，既愈，入謝，帝 曰：「舅久不覿太皇太后，宜少憩內東門，朕當自啟。」

translations.literal: During Yuanfeng he reported illness; when recovered he came to give thanks, and the Emperor said: "Uncle, you have long not seen the Grand Empress Dowager; you should rest briefly at the inner eastern gate, and I shall announce you myself."
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfeng he reported illness; when he recovered and came to give thanks, the Emperor said: "Uncle, you have not seen the Grand Empress Dowager in a long while. Rest briefly at the inner eastern gate, and I shall announce you myself."

sentences.zh: 已而召入，曆上下儒釋道五閣、大椿蟠桃亭，再升殿乃退。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned in, passed through the five halls of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism upstairs and downstairs and the Great Paulownia Peach Pavilion, and only after ascending the hall twice did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was summoned in and conducted through the five halls of Confucianism, Buddhism, and Daoism upstairs and downstairs and the Great Paulownia Peach Pavilion. Only after ascending the hall twice did he withdraw.

sentences.zh: 以護國軍節度使、司徒兼中書令為中太一宮使， 給朱衣雙引騎吏前馬。

translations.literal: As Military Governor of Huguo Army, Minister of Education and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat he became Director of the Central Great Unity Palace, granted vermilion robes, double escorts, and mounted attendants preceding his horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military governor of Huguo Army, minister of education, and concurrent director of the Secretariat, and appointed director of the Central Great Unity Palace, with vermilion robes, double escorts, and mounted attendants preceding his horse.

sentences.zh: 慈聖喪終，請郡，帝曰：「時見舅如麵慶壽宮，奈何欲遠朕，得無禮遇有不至乎？」

translations.literal: When Empress Cisheng's mourning ended, he requested a provincial post. The Emperor said: "When I see Uncle it is as if face to face at Shouqing Palace — why would you wish to be far from me? Could it be that in some courtesy you have been treated insufficiently?"
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Cisheng's mourning period ended, he requested a provincial post. The Emperor said: "Seeing you, Uncle, is like meeting face to face at Shouqing Palace — why would you wish to go far from me? Could it be you felt some courtesy was lacking?"

sentences.zh: 佾皇恐。

translations.literal: Cao Yi was filled with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 即城南為園池，給八作兵庀役，疏 惠民河水灌之，且將為築三百楹第，固辭乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the southern suburbs he was given a garden and pond, laborers from the Eight Works Bureau for construction, and the Huimin River was dredged to irrigate it; they were also about to build for him a residence of three hundred bays, but he firmly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a garden and pond were prepared for him in the southern suburbs, laborers from the Eight Works Bureau were assigned to the task, and the Huimin River was dredged to irrigate it. The court also planned to build him a residence of three hundred bays, but he firmly declined and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 高麗獻玉帶，為秋蘆白鷺紋極精巧，詔後苑工以黃金仿其制為帶，賜佾。

translations.literal: Goryeo presented a jade belt with autumn-reed and white-egret patterns of extreme refinement; an edict ordered craftsmen of the imperial rear garden to imitate it in gold as a belt and grant it to Cao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo presented a jade belt with autumn-reed and white-egret patterns of extraordinary refinement. An edict ordered craftsmen of the imperial rear garden to reproduce it in gold as a belt and grant it to Cao Yi.

sentences.zh: 生日，賚予如宰相、親王，用教坊樂工服色 衣侑酒，以示尊寵。

translations.literal: On his birthday, gifts were bestowed equal to those for chief ministers and imperial princes; palace musicians in colored robes were used to offer wine, to show special honor.
translations.idiomatic: On his birthday he received gifts equal to those given chief ministers and imperial princes, with palace musicians in colored robes offering wine to show his special honor.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，加少保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, he was promoted to junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 坤成節獻壽，特綴宰相班，優詔減拜。

translations.literal: On the Kunshao Festival he presented birthday felicitations, was specially placed after the chief ministers' ranks, and received an edict graciously reducing the bowing required.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kunshao Festival he presented birthday felicitations, was specially placed after the chief ministers' ranks, and received an edict graciously reducing the required bows.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈太師，追封沂王。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two, was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor, and posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two, was posthumously made grand preceptor, and posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 從弟偕，子評、誘。

translations.literal: His cousin was Xie; his sons were Ping and You.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin was Xie; his sons were Ping and You.

sentences.zh: 偕字光道，少讀書知義，以節俠自喜。

translations.literal: Xie, courtesy name Guangdao, in youth read books and knew righteousness, and took pride in his chivalrous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, courtesy name Guangdao, read books from youth and understood righteousness, and took pride in his chivalrous spirit.

sentences.zh: 為許州都監，幕客史沆傾險，劫持為不法，上下畏之。

translations.literal: While serving as Chief Supervisor of Xu Prefecture, his staff member Shi Hang was treacherous and overbearing, forcing others into unlawful acts; both superiors and subordinates feared him.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as chief supervisor of Xu Prefecture, his staff member Shi Hang was treacherous and domineering, coercing others into unlawful acts, and both superiors and subordinates feared him.

sentences.zh: 偕從容置酒，對客數沆十罪，將擊殺之，沆起拜謝，偕罵曰：「復不 改，必殺汝。」

translations.literal: Xie calmly set out wine; before guests he enumerated ten crimes of Hang and was about to kill him; Hang rose and bowed in apology; Xie cursed: "If you do not change again, I shall surely kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Xie calmly set out wine and, before his guests, listed ten crimes of Hang and was about to kill him. Hang rose and bowed in apology. Xie cursed: "If you do not reform, I shall surely kill you."

sentences.zh: 沆為斂跡。

translations.literal: Hang thereupon restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hang thereupon reined himself in.

sentences.zh: 累遷東上閣門使、帶禦器械、知雄州。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate, Bearer of Imperial Arms, and Prefect of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to commissioner of the eastern upper gate, bearer of imperial arms, and prefect of Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 議者欲廢塘濼為田，偕曰：「何承矩、李允則營此累年，所以限契丹，廢之不可。」

translations.literal: Critics wished to abandon the pond-polders for farmland; Xie said: "He Chengjui and Li Yunze built these over many years precisely to hem in the Khitans; they must not be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: When critics proposed abandoning the pond-polders for farmland, Xie said: "He Chengjui and Li Yunze spent years building these to block the Khitans. They must not be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 進華州防禦 使、知相州，徙河陽總管，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Defender of Hua Prefecture and Prefect of Xiang Prefecture, transferred to Grand Administrator of Heyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defender of Hua Prefecture and prefect of Xiang Prefecture, transferred to grand administrator of Heyang, and died.

sentences.zh: 嘗從梅堯臣學詩，堯臣稱之，為序其詩。

translations.literal: Once he studied poetry under Mei Yaochen; Yaochen praised him and wrote a preface to his poems.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied poetry under Mei Yaochen. Yaochen praised him and wrote a preface to his poems.

sentences.zh: 性喜文史，書有楷法。

translations.literal: By nature he loved literature and history, and his calligraphy had standard form.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved literature and history, and his calligraphy was in standard form.

sentences.zh: 慈聖命書屏以奉，神宗即賜玉帶旌其能。

translations.literal: Empress Cisheng ordered him to write screens for presentation; Emperor Shenzong immediately bestowed a jade belt to honor his skill.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Cisheng ordered him to write screens for presentation, and Emperor Shenzong immediately bestowed a jade belt to honor his ability.

sentences.zh: 尤善射，左右手如一，夜或滅燭能中。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at archery; left and right hand were alike; at night he could sometimes extinguish the candle and still hit the target.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at archery; his left and right hands were equally good, and even at night with the candles extinguished he could still hit the target.

sentences.zh: 伴契丹使者射，嘗雙破的，客驚竦。

translations.literal: While accompanying Khitan envoys in archery, he once hit both targets and the guests were startled and awed.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying Khitan envoys in archery, he once hit both targets, leaving the guests startled and awed.

sentences.zh: 在戚裏號為湛厚。

translations.literal: Among imperial kinsmen he was known as deep and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Among imperial kinsmen he was known for depth and generosity.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously granted Grand Master with the same ceremony as the Three Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously granted grand master with ceremonial standing equal to the Three Councillors.

sentences.zh: 誘字公善，以蔭至左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: You, courtesy name Gongshan, through hereditary privilege rose to Deputy Director of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: You, courtesy name Gongshan, through hereditary privilege rose to deputy director of the left treasury.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，父佾以疾告入謝，神宗麵授誘閣門通事舍人。

translations.literal: During Xining, his father Yi reported illness and came to give thanks; Emperor Shenzong personally appointed You as Gate Attendant and Imperial Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, his father Yi reported illness and came to give thanks; Emperor Shenzong personally appointed You gate attendant and imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，以東上閣門使為真定府、定州路兵馬鈐轄，遷文州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, as Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate he served as Military Controller of Zhending Prefecture and Dingzhou Circuit, and was promoted to Prefect of Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, as commissioner of the eastern upper gate he served as military controller of Zhending Prefecture and the Dingzhou Circuit, and was promoted to prefect of Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，至其宮門，館客者下馬邀誘同入，誘曰：「北朝使至，及朝堂門，兩朝積好久，無妄生事。」

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to the Khitans, upon reaching their palace gate the host guest-official dismounted and invited You to enter with him; You said: "When envoys of the Northern Court arrive, they do not dismount until the court hall gate; the two courts have long been at peace — let us not rashly create trouble."
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitans, when he reached their palace gate the host official dismounted and invited You to enter with him. You said: "When envoys of the Northern Court arrive, they do not dismount until the court hall gate. The two courts have long been on good terms — let us not rashly create trouble."

sentences.zh: 卒乘馬入。

translations.literal: In the end he entered riding his horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he entered on horseback.

sentences.zh: 使還，為樞密副都承旨。

translations.literal: Upon returning from his mission, he became Deputy Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning from his mission, he became deputy chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時，進都承旨。

translations.literal: During Huizong's reign he was promoted to Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During Huizong's reign he was promoted to chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 曆 慶州團練、恩州防禦、晉州觀察使，保慶軍留後。

translations.literal: He successively served as Regimental Commander of Qing Prefecture, Defender of En Prefecture, Inspector of Jin Prefecture, and Acting Military Governor of Baoqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as regimental commander of Qing Prefecture, defender of En Prefecture, inspector of Jin Prefecture, and acting military governor of Baoqing Army.

sentences.zh: 大觀中，進安德軍節度使、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: During the Daguang period he was promoted to Military Governor of Andre Army and Director of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daguang period he was promoted to military governor of Andre Army and director of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 與兄評同日拜，立雙節堂於家，戚裏榮之。

translations.literal: On the same day he and his elder brother Ping received appointments; they established a Twin Credentials Hall at home, and imperial kinsmen honored them for it.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Ping received appointments on the same day and established a Twin Credentials Hall at home, to the admiration of the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 性謹密，習熟典故。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious and meticulous; he was practiced and familiar with precedents.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was cautious and meticulous, and well versed in precedents and protocol.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠定。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-five, was posthumously granted Grand Master with the same ceremony as the Three Councillors, and given the posthumous title Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five, was posthumously granted grand master with ceremonial standing equal to the Three Councillors, and given the posthumous title Zhongding.

sentences.zh: 高遵裕，字公綽，忠武軍節度使瓊之孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Zunyu, courtesy name Gongchuo, was the grandson of Military Governor of Zhongwu Army Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zunyu, courtesy name Gongchuo, was the grandson of military governor of Zhongwu Army Qiong.

sentences.zh: 以父任累遷供備庫副使、鎮戎軍駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Through his father's position he was successively promoted to Deputy Director of the Equipment Supply Office and Chief Supervisor of the Garrison at Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position he was successively promoted to deputy director of the equipment supply office and chief supervisor of the garrison at Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇大順城，諒祚中矢遁。

translations.literal: The Tangut raided Dashun City, and Liangzuo was struck by an arrow and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut raided Dashun City, and Liangzuo was struck by an arrow and fled.

sentences.zh: 會英宗晏駕，遣遵裕告哀，抵宥州下宮，夏人 遣王盥受命，以吉服至，遵裕切責之，遂易服。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Yingzong died; Zunyu was sent to announce the mourning. Reaching the lower palace at You Prefecture, the Tangut sent Wang Guan to receive the message, arriving in auspicious dress; Zunyu sternly rebuked him, and he thereupon changed his dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong died, Zunyu was sent to announce the mourning. Reaching the lower palace at You Prefecture, the Tangut dispatched Wang Guan to receive the message in festive dress. Zunyu sternly rebuked him, and Wang Guan changed his attire.

sentences.zh: 既而具食上宮，語及大順城事，盥曰：「剽掠輩耳。」

translations.literal: Thereupon a feast was prepared at the upper palace; when the matter of Dashun City was mentioned, Guan said: "Mere plunderers."
translations.idiomatic: A feast was then prepared at the upper palace. When the matter of Dashun City came up, Guan said: "They were mere plunderers."

sentences.zh: 遵裕曰：「若主寇邊，扶傷而循，斯言非妄邪！」

translations.literal: Zunyu said: "If your ruler raided the border, supporting the wounded as he withdrew — is this statement not false!"
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu replied: "If your ruler raided the border and withdrew while supporting the wounded, is this not a false statement?"

sentences.zh: 夏人以為 辱，亟遣人代對，終食不敢發口，輒忿怒曰：「王人蔑視下國，弊邑雖小，控弦十數萬，亦能躬執橐，與君周旋。」

translations.literal: The Tangut considered this an insult and quickly sent someone to reply in his place; through the entire meal he dared not speak, but then in anger said: "The envoy of the Son of Heaven despises our humble state; though our small domain has only a hundred thousand bowmen, we too can personally take up arms and contend with you."
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut took this as an insult and quickly sent someone to reply in Guan's place. Through the entire meal Guan dared not speak, but then burst out in anger: "The envoy of the Son of Heaven despises our humble state. Though our small domain can field only a hundred thousand bowmen, we too can take up arms and contend with you."

sentences.zh: 遵裕瞋目曰：「主上天縱神武，毋肆狂蹶，以幹 誅夷。」

translations.literal: Zunyu glared and said: "Our ruler is endowed by Heaven with divine martial prowess — do not indulge in reckless insolence and invite extermination."
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu glared and said: "Our ruler is endowed by Heaven with divine martial prowess. Do not indulge in reckless insolence and invite extermination."

sentences.zh: 時諒祚覘於屏間，搖手使止。

translations.literal: At that time Liangzuo was peering from behind a screen and waved his hand to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Liangzuo was peering from behind a screen and waved his hand for him to stop.

sentences.zh: 神宗聞而嘉之，擢知保安軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong heard of this he praised him and promoted him to command Bao'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong heard of this he praised him and promoted him to command Bao'an Army.

sentences.zh: 橫山豪欲向化，帝使遵裕諭種諤圖之。

translations.literal: A powerful man of Hengshan wished to submit; the Emperor had Zunyu instruct Zhong E to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: When a powerful leader of Hengshan wished to submit, the Emperor had Zunyu instruct Zhong E to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 諤遂取綏州。

translations.literal: E thereupon seized Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E thereupon seized Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 帥怒諤擅發兵，欲正軍法，諤懼，稱得密旨於遵裕，故諤被罪，遵裕亦降為乾州都監。

translations.literal: The commander was angry that E had mobilized troops on his own authority and wished to apply military law; E feared this and claimed he had received a secret order from Zunyu; therefore E was punished, and Zunyu was also demoted to Chief Supervisor of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The commander was angered that Zhong E had mobilized troops without authorization and wished to apply military law. Zhong E, fearing punishment, claimed he had received a secret order from Zunyu. Zhong E was punished, and Zunyu was demoted to chief supervisor of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷通事舍人，主管西路羌部，駐古渭砦，分所部羌兵為三等，教為軍法。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Messenger, put in charge of the western Qiang tribes, stationed at Guwei Stockade, divided the Qiang troops under his command into three grades, and trained them in military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to imperial messenger, put in charge of the western Qiang tribes, and stationed at Guwei Stockade. He divided the Qiang troops under his command into three grades and trained them in military regulations.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，朝廷用王韶復洮、隴，命為秦鳳路沿邊安撫，以遵裕副之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining the court employed Wang Shao to recover Tao and Long, appointing him Frontier Pacification Commissioner of Qin-Feng Circuit, with Zunyu as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining the court employed Wang Shao to recover Tao and Long, appointing him frontier pacification commissioner of the Qin-Feng Circuit, with Zunyu as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋以古渭為通遠軍，命知軍事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Guwei was made Tongyuan Army, and he was ordered to command its military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Guwei was made Tongyuan Army, and he was ordered to command its military affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，持附順羌部圖籍及繪青唐、武勝形勢入獻，擢引進副 使、帶禦器械，俾歸治師。

translations.literal: The next year he presented registers of submitted Qiang tribes and maps of the terrain of Qingtang and Wusheng; he was promoted to Deputy Introducing Commissioner and Bearer of Imperial Arms, and sent back to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he presented registers of submitted Qiang tribes and maps of the terrain of Qingtang and Wusheng. He was promoted to deputy introducing commissioner and bearer of imperial arms, and sent back to command the army.

sentences.zh: 師次慶平堡，夜行，晨至野人關，羌人旅拒，引親兵一鼓破之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Qingping Fort, marched by night, and at dawn reached Yeren Pass; the Qiang massed to resist, but he led his personal troops and broke them in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Qingping Fort, marched by night, and at dawn reached Yeren Pass. The Qiang massed to resist, but he led his personal troops and broke them in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 進營武勝城下，羌眾逃去，遂據其城。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped below Wusheng City; the Qiang masses fled, and he thereupon occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped below Wusheng City. The Qiang masses fled, and he occupied the city.

sentences.zh: 詔建為鎮洮軍，又命知軍事。

translations.literal: An edict established it as Zhentao Army, and again ordered him to command its military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established it as Zhentao Army and again ordered him to command its military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋以 熙、河、洮、岷、通遠為一路，進西上閣門使、榮州刺史，充總管，復知通遠軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan were made one circuit; he was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate and Prefect of Rong Prefecture, appointed overall commander, and again commanded Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xi, He, Tao, Min, and Tongyuan were made one circuit. He was promoted to commissioner of the western upper gate and prefect of Rong Prefecture, appointed overall commander, and again placed in command of Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 明年，韶欲取河州，遵裕曰：「古渭舉事，先建堡砦，以漸而進，故一舉拔武勝。

translations.literal: The next year Shao wished to take He Prefecture; Zunyu said: "When we acted at Guwei, we first built forts and stockades and advanced step by step, and so in one effort we took Wusheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shao wished to take He Prefecture. Zunyu said: "When we acted at Guwei, we first built forts and stockades and advanced step by step, and so in one effort we took Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 今兵與糧未備，一旦越數舍圖人之地，使彼阻要害，我軍進退無所矣。」

translations.literal: Now troops and provisions are not ready; if in one stroke we cross several stages into enemy territory and they block the strategic points, our army will have nowhere to advance or retreat."
translations.idiomatic: Now troops and provisions are not ready. If in one stroke we cross several stages into enemy territory and they block the strategic points, our army will have nowhere to advance or retreat."

sentences.zh: 韶與李憲笑曰：「君何遽相異邪？」

translations.literal: Shao and Li Xian laughed and said: "Why do you suddenly differ from us?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao and Li Xian laughed and said: "Why do you suddenly disagree with us?"

sentences.zh: 檄使守臨洮。

translations.literal: By written order he was made to guard Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: By written order he was made to guard Lintao.

sentences.zh: 韶攻河州，果不克。

translations.literal: Shao attacked He Prefecture and indeed failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao attacked He Prefecture and indeed failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 帝善遵裕議，令專管洮、岷、疊、岩未款附者。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved Zunyu's proposal and ordered him to take charge exclusively of those in Tao, Min, Die, and Yan who had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved Zunyu's proposal and ordered him to take charge exclusively of those in Tao, Min, Die, and Yan who had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 遵裕以俞龍珂地有鹽井，遂築鹽川砦。

translations.literal: Zunyu, because Yu Longke's territory had salt wells, thereupon built Yanchuan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yu Longke's territory had salt wells, Zunyu built Yanchuan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 瞎吳叱率諸羌脅青唐，欲擾邊，詔遣張玉攻討。

translations.literal: Xia Wuchi led the various Qiang to coerce Qingtang and intended to disturb the border; an edict dispatched Zhang Yu to attack and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Wuchi led the various Qiang to coerce Qingtang and intended to disturb the border. An edict dispatched Zhang Yu to attack and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 遵裕曰：「青唐無罪，第為生羌所脅耳。」

translations.literal: Zunyu said: "Qingtang is not guilty; it is merely coerced by the raw Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu said: "Qingtang is not guilty; it is merely coerced by the raw Qiang."

sentences.zh: 遣裨將與龍珂率眾禦之。

translations.literal: He dispatched a subordinate general with Longke to lead troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched a subordinate general with Longke to lead troops in resistance.

sentences.zh: 青唐人 見龍珂泣訴，瞎吳叱知不附己，潰去。

translations.literal: When the people of Qingtang saw Longke they wept and appealed; Xia Wuchi knew they would not follow him and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Qingtang saw Longke they wept and appealed to him. Xia Wuchi knew they would not follow him and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 從韶取岷州，下之，令士眾曰：「生獲老幼與得級同。」

translations.literal: Following Shao he took Min Prefecture and captured it; he ordered the troops: "Capturing the living, old and young, counts the same as taking heads."
translations.idiomatic: Following Shao he took Min Prefecture. He ordered the troops: "Capturing the living, old and young, counts the same as taking heads."

sentences.zh: 全活者以數萬。

translations.literal: Those wholly spared numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Those spared numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，加岷州刺史。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to Prefect of Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to prefect of Min Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，羌乘景思立 之敗，圍河、岷二州，道路不通者幾月。

translations.literal: The next year the Qiang, taking advantage of Jing Sil's defeat, besieged He and Min Prefectures, and the roads were blocked for nearly several months.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Qiang, taking advantage of Jing Sil's defeat, besieged He and Min Prefectures, and the roads were blocked for nearly several months.

sentences.zh: 或請退保，遵裕曰：「敢議此者斬！」

translations.literal: Some requested withdrawing to a defensive position; Zunyu said: "Whoever dares discuss this shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed withdrawing to a defensive position. Zunyu said: "Whoever dares discuss this shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 岷城軍缺，守者恐，遵裕登西門，命將縱擊，別選精騎由南門噪而出，合擊之，羌敗 走。

translations.literal: The garrison at Min City was short; the defenders were afraid. Zunyu mounted the western gate, ordered the generals to strike freely, separately selected elite cavalry to charge out noisily from the southern gate, and joined in the attack; the Qiang were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Min City was understrength and the defenders were afraid. Zunyu mounted the western gate, ordered the generals to strike freely, and separately selected elite cavalry to charge out noisily from the southern gate. The combined attack defeated the Qiang and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以岷城遠難守，議棄之。

translations.literal: At that time the court, because Min City was distant and hard to hold, debated abandoning it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court debated abandoning Min City because it was distant and hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 詔至，賊已潰矣。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, the enemy had already dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, the enemy had already dispersed.

sentences.zh: 以功進團練使、龍神衛都指揮使、知熙州。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Regimental Commander, Commander-in-Chief of the Dragon Divine Guard, and Prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to regimental commander, commander-in-chief of the Dragon Divine Guard, and prefect of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐薦張穆之為轉運使，而穆之有罪，罷知潁州，未幾，徙慶州，又 坐事黜知淮陽軍。

translations.literal: Because he had recommended Zhang Muzhi as transport commissioner and Muzhi was guilty, he was dismissed from Ying Prefecture; before long he was transferred to Qing Prefecture, and again because of an offense was demoted to command Huaiyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had recommended Zhang Muzhi as transport commissioner and Muzhi was found guilty, he was dismissed from Ying Prefecture. Before long he was transferred to Qing Prefecture, and again because of an offense was demoted to command Huaiyang Army.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，復知慶州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng he again commanded Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng he again commanded Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔與諸路討夏國。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to join the various circuits in campaigning against the Xia state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to join the various circuits in campaigning against the Xia state.

sentences.zh: 請濟師，得東兵十一將，騎不足用，以群牧馬益之。

translations.literal: He requested reinforcements and received eleven eastern generals; cavalry was insufficient, so horses from the imperial stud were added.
translations.idiomatic: He requested reinforcements and received eleven eastern generals. Cavalry was insufficient, so horses from the imperial stud were added.

sentences.zh: 又令節制涇原兵，劉昌祚先至靈州，幾得城，遵裕嫉之，故不用其計，遂以潰歸，語在《昌祚傳》。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to command the Jingyuan troops. Liu Changzuo arrived first at Ling Prefecture and nearly took the city; Zunyu envied him and therefore did not use his plan, and so they collapsed in retreat — the account is in the Biography of Changzuo.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to command the Jingyuan troops. Liu Changzuo arrived first at Ling Prefecture and nearly took the city, but Zunyu envied him and therefore did not use his plan. The army collapsed in retreat — the account is in the "Biography of Changzuo."

sentences.zh: 貶郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Deputy Regimental Commander of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to deputy regimental commander of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遵惠字子育，以蔭為供奉官。

translations.literal: Zunhui, courtesy name Ziyu, through hereditary privilege became a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zunhui, courtesy name Ziyu, through hereditary privilege became a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，試經義中選，換大理評事。

translations.literal: During Xining he passed the examination in classical meaning and was changed to Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining he passed the examination in classical meaning and was appointed assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 曆三班院主簿、軍器丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Registrar of the Three-Ranks Bureau and Assistant Director of the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as registrar of the Three-Ranks Bureau and assistant director of the armory.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，上疏言：「法度更張，事有當否，如先帝所施設，未可輕議。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he submitted a memorial, stating: "When laws and institutions are changed, some matters are right and some wrong; such things as the late emperor established should not be lightly debated."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou he submitted a memorial, saying: "When laws and institutions are changed, some measures are right and some wrong. What the late emperor established should not be lightly debated."

sentences.zh: 擢太僕少卿，上太府卿，出知河中府，改河北路都轉運使，未行，拜工部侍郎，以集賢殿 修撰知鄆州、河南、穎昌府，加寶文閣待制、知成德軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, then Director of the Imperial Treasury; he went out to command Hezhong Prefecture, was changed to Overall Transport Commissioner of Hebei Circuit but did not take up the post; he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, and as Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies commanded Yan, Henan, and Yingchang Prefectures; he was additionally made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Precious Culture and commanded Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial Stud and then director of the Imperial Treasury. He went out to command Hezhong Prefecture, was appointed overall transport commissioner of the Hebei Circuit but did not take up the post, and was made vice minister of works. As academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies he commanded Yan, Henan, and Yingchang Prefectures, was additionally made attendant gentleman of the Hall of Precious Culture, and commanded Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部侍郎，以龍圖閣學士知慶州。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and as Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams commanded Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of revenue and, as academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, commanded Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，贈樞密直學士。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously granted Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously granted academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 方宣仁後臨朝，繩檢族人一以法度，乃舉家事付遵惠，遵惠躬表率之，人無間言。

translations.literal: When Empress Xuanren held court, she restrained her clansmen entirely by law; she entrusted family affairs to Zunhui, and Zunhui personally set the example, and no one had anything to say against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xuanren held court, she restrained her clansmen entirely by law. She entrusted family affairs to Zunhui, who personally set the example, and no one found fault with him.

sentences.zh: 亦能遠嫌自保，故不罹紹聖之禍。

translations.literal: He was also able to keep his distance from suspicion and protect himself, and so did not suffer the calamity of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was also able to keep his distance from suspicion and protect himself, and so did not suffer the calamity of the Shaosheng period.

sentences.zh: 從侄士林。

translations.literal: His cousin was Shilin.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin was Shilin.

sentences.zh: 士林字才卿，宣仁聖烈皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Shilin, courtesy name Caiqing, was the younger brother of Empress Xuanren Shengli.
translations.idiomatic: Shilin, courtesy name Caiqing, was the younger brother of Empress Xuanren Shengli.

sentences.zh: 累官內殿崇班、殿直，英宗書「謹守法律」四字誨之曰：「能此則為良吏矣。」

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Honored Officer of the Inner Hall and Palace Attendant; Emperor Yingzong wrote the four characters "Strictly Observe the Law" and instructed him, saying: "If you can do this you will be a good official."
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the posts of honored officer of the inner hall and palace attendant. Emperor Yingzong wrote the four characters "Strictly Observe the Law" and instructed him: "If you can do this you will be a good official."

sentences.zh: 每欲進擢，後屢辭輒止。

translations.literal: Whenever promotion was intended, the Empress repeatedly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever promotion was intended, the empress repeatedly declined and it was stopped.

sentences.zh: 喜儒學，涉閱經史， 通大義，尤有巧智。

translations.literal: He loved Confucian learning, read widely in the classics and histories, understood the larger principles, and was especially ingenious.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Confucian learning, read widely in the classics and histories, understood larger principles, and was especially ingenious.

sentences.zh: 嘗監揚州召伯閘稅，木舊用火印，士林改刃其印文，鑿以為識，尤簡便，傍郡皆效焉。

translations.literal: Once while supervising the tax at Zhaobo Lock in Yang Prefecture, the old method used fire brands on wood; Shilin changed the cutting of the seal characters and carved them as marks, which was especially convenient, and neighboring prefectures all imitated it.
translations.idiomatic: Once while supervising the tax at Zhaobo Lock in Yang Prefecture, the old method used fire brands on wood. Shilin changed the cutting of the seal characters and carved them as marks, which was especially convenient, and neighboring prefectures all imitated the method.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈德州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Prefect of De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted prefect of De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，加贈昭德軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, he was further posthumously granted Military Governor of Zhaode Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, he was further posthumously granted military governor of Zhaode Army.

sentences.zh: 紹興初， 追封普安郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pu'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Pu'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子公紀。

translations.literal: His son was Gongji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gongji.

sentences.zh: 公紀字君正，曆閣門祗候、通事舍人，累進寧州刺史、團練使、永州防禦使、集慶留後。

translations.literal: Gongji, courtesy name Junzheng, successively served as Gate Attendant and Imperial Messenger, and was promoted to Prefect of Ning Prefecture, Regimental Commander, Defender of Yong Prefecture, and Acting Military Governor of Jiqing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gongji, courtesy name Junzheng, successively served as gate attendant and imperial messenger, and was promoted to prefect of Ning Prefecture, regimental commander, defender of Yong Prefecture, and acting military governor of Jiqing Army.

sentences.zh: 性儉約，珍異聲伎無所好，奉祿多以給諸族，得任子恩，均及孤遠。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and abstemious, had no fondness for rare objects or music and performers, and mostly used his salary to support the various clans; when he received the privilege of appointing a son to office, he distributed it equally even to the isolated and distant.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and abstemious, had no fondness for rare objects or entertainers, and mostly used his salary to support the various clans. When he received the privilege of appointing a son to office, he distributed it equally even to the isolated and distant.

sentences.zh: 持宣仁後喪未終，卒，贈感德軍節度使，諡曰懷僖。

translations.literal: While still observing mourning for Empress Xuanren he died; he was posthumously granted Military Governor of Gande Army with the posthumous title Huaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: While still observing mourning for Empress Xuanren he died. He was posthumously made military governor of Gande Army and given the posthumous title Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，追封新興郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Xinxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子世則。

translations.literal: His son was Shize.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shize.

sentences.zh: 世則字仲貽，幼以恩補左班殿直，至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Shize, courtesy name Zhongyi, in youth through privilege was appointed Left Watch Commander and rose to Honored Officer of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shize, courtesy name Zhongyi, in youth through privilege was appointed left watch commander and rose to honored officer of the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 復用父遺表恩為閣門祗候，後除親衛郎。

translations.literal: Again using the privilege from his father's death memorial he became Gate Attendant, and later was appointed Personal Guard Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Again using the privilege from his father's death memorial he became gate attendant, and later was appointed personal guard officer.

sentences.zh: 以通經典，轉內殿承製。

translations.literal: Because he was versed in the classics, he was transferred to Inner Hall Document Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was versed in the classics, he was transferred to inner hall document drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 累遷康州防禦使，知西上閣門事。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Defender of Kang Prefecture and put in charge of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to defender of Kang Prefecture and put in charge of the western upper gate.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，金泛使至，徽宗命世則掌客。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe, when Jin envoys arrived in large numbers, Emperor Huizong ordered Shize to manage guest affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanhe, when Jin envoys arrived in large numbers, Emperor Huizong ordered Shize to manage guest affairs.

sentences.zh: 世則記問該洽，應對有據，帝聞，悅之，自是掌客多命世則。

translations.literal: Shize's memory and knowledge were comprehensive and his responses well grounded; when the Emperor heard of this he was pleased, and from then on guest affairs were mostly entrusted to Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Shize's memory and knowledge were comprehensive and his responses well grounded. When the Emperor heard of this he was pleased, and from then on guest affairs were mostly entrusted to Shize.

sentences.zh: 金人軍城下，又命世則使其軍，還，進秩二等，遷知東上閣門 使。

translations.literal: When the Jin army besieged the city, he was again ordered to go as envoy to their army; upon returning he was promoted two ranks and transferred to Commissioner of the Eastern Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army besieged the city, he was again ordered to go as envoy to their army. Upon returning he was promoted two ranks and transferred to commissioner of the eastern upper gate.

sentences.zh: 金遣燕人吳孝民請和，孝民邀宰執、親王詣軍前議事，高宗在康邸，請行。

translations.literal: The Jin sent the Yan man Wu Xiaomin to sue for peace; Xiaomin invited the chief ministers and imperial princes to come before the army to discuss affairs; Gaozong was at the Prince of Kang's residence and requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent the Yan man Wu Xiaomin to sue for peace. Xiaomin invited the chief ministers and imperial princes to come before the army to discuss affairs. Gaozong was at the Prince of Kang's residence and requested to go.

sentences.zh: 是日，世則入對，遂除計議副使以從。

translations.literal: That day Shize entered for audience and was thereupon appointed Deputy Planning Commissioner to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shize entered for audience and was thereupon appointed deputy planning commissioner to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 康王復使河北，世則改華州觀察使，充參議 官。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Kang was again sent to Hebei, Shize was changed to Inspector of Hua Prefecture and served as Advisory Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang was again sent to Hebei, Shize was changed to inspector of Hua Prefecture and served as advisory officer.

sentences.zh: 召對，賜金帶。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was granted a golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was granted a golden belt.

sentences.zh: 當高宗艱難中，世則嘗在左右，寢處不少離。

translations.literal: During Gaozong's hardships, Shize was often at his side and rarely left him day or night.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozong's hardships, Shize was often at his side and rarely left him day or night.

sentences.zh: 大元帥府建，改元帥府參議官，因請布檄諸路，以定人心。

translations.literal: When the Grand Marshal's Office was established, he was changed to Advisory Officer of the Grand Marshal's Office and requested that proclamations be issued to the various circuits to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Marshal's Office was established, he was changed to advisory officer of the Grand Marshal's Office and requested that proclamations be issued to the various circuits to settle the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 進遙郡承宣使，不拜。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Distant-Commandery Commissioner-in-Chief but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to distant-commandery commissioner-in-chief but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 高宗承製，轉越州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Inspector of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to inspector of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及即位，除保靜軍承宣使，提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Shize was appointed Commissioner-in-Chief of Baojing Army and put in charge of Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Shize was appointed commissioner-in-chief of Baojing Army and put in charge of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 詔令編類元帥府事跡付史館，召為樞密都承旨兼提舉京畿監牧，再提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the compilation of the Grand Marshal's Office records to be sent to the Historiography Office; he was recalled as Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently put in charge of the capital-region stud farms, and again put in charge of Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the compilation of the Grand Marshal's Office records to be sent to the Historiography Office. He was recalled as chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently put in charge of the capital-region stud farms, and again put in charge of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 世則居溫州，帝遣中使諭守臣以時給奉祿，凡積二萬緡，因請以裨郡費。

translations.literal: Shize resided in Wen Prefecture; the Emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct the local officials to pay his salary on time; in all twenty thousand strings had accumulated, and he requested that it be used to supplement the prefectural expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shize resided in Wen Prefecture. The Emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct the local officials to pay his salary on time. In all twenty thousand strings had accumulated, and he requested that it be used to supplement the prefectural expenses.

sentences.zh: 常病瘍，艱於據鞍，又以舊所禦肩輿賜焉。

translations.literal: He often suffered from sores and had difficulty mounting a saddle; the old palanquin he had used was also bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He often suffered from sores and had difficulty mounting a saddle. The old palanquin he had used was also bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 帝每念宣仁聖烈皇后保祐三朝，中遭誣詆，外 家班秩無顯者，製以為感德軍節度使，充萬壽觀使，進開府儀同三司，奉朝請，賜第臨安。

translations.literal: The Emperor often recalled that Empress Xuanren Shengli had protected three reigns yet in the midst of it suffered slander; no one of the maternal kin held conspicuous rank; he was appointed Military Governor of Gande Army, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey, promoted to Grand Master with the same ceremony as the Three Councillors, granted attendance at court, and given a residence in Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often recalled that Empress Xuanren Shengli had protected three reigns yet in the midst of it suffered slander, and that no one of the maternal kin held conspicuous rank. Shize was appointed military governor of Gande Army, put in charge of Wanshou Abbey, promoted to grand master with ceremonial standing equal to the Three Councillors, granted attendance at court, and given a residence in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 除景靈宮使，兼判溫州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Jingling Palace and concurrently given charge of Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of Jingling Palace and concurrently given charge of Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋以病丐罷，後為萬壽觀使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, citing illness, he requested to be relieved; later he served as Director of Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing illness, he requested to be relieved. Later he served as director of Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 十四年，召入覲， 進少保，懇求還。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned to audience, promoted to Junior Guardian, and earnestly requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was summoned to audience, promoted to junior guardian, and earnestly requested to return.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈太傅，賜田三十頃，諡曰忠節。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-five, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, granted thirty qing of land, and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five, was posthumously made grand preceptor, granted thirty qing of land, and given the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 向傳範，字仲模，尚書左僕射敏中之子。

translations.literal: Xiang Chuanfan, courtesy name Zhongmo, was the son of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Chuanfan, courtesy name Zhongmo, was the son of left vice director of the Department of State Affairs Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 以父任為衛尉丞。

translations.literal: Through his father's position he became Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position he became assistant director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 娶南陽郡王惟吉女，改內殿崇班、帶禦器械，曆知相、恩、邢三州。

translations.literal: He married the daughter of Prince of Nanyang Weiji, was changed to Honored Officer of the Inner Hall and Bearer of Imperial Arms, and successively served as Prefect of Xiang, En, and Xing Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He married the daughter of Prince of Nanyang Weiji, was changed to honored officer of the inner hall and bearer of imperial arms, and successively served as prefect of Xiang, En, and Xing Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入管幹客省、閣門、皇城司。

translations.literal: He entered to manage the Office of Foreign Guests, the Gate Office, and the Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered to manage the Office of Foreign Guests, the Gate Office, and the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 知陝州，仁宗賜詩以寵其行。

translations.literal: He commanded Shaan Prefecture; Emperor Renzong bestowed a poem to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Shaan Prefecture, and Emperor Renzong bestowed a poem to honor his departure.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，知鄆州兼京東西路安撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining he commanded Yan Prefecture and concurrently served as Pacification Commissioner of the Jingdong and Jingxi Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining he commanded Yan Prefecture and concurrently served as pacification commissioner of the Jingdong and Jingxi Circuits.

sentences.zh: 諫官楊繪言：「傳範領安撫使，無以杜外戚僥求之源。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Yang Hui said: "Chuanfan holding the post of pacification commissioner does nothing to block the source of opportunistic requests by imperial kinsmen."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Yang Hui said: "Chuanfan holding the post of pacification commissioner does nothing to block the source of opportunistic requests by imperial kinsmen."

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博曰：「傳範累典郡，非緣外戚。」

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner Wen Yanbo said: "Chuanfan has repeatedly commanded prefectures — this is not because of imperial kinship."
translations.idiomatic: Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Wen Yanbo said: "Chuanfan has repeatedly commanded prefectures — this is not because of imperial kinship."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「得諫官如此言，甚善，可以止他日妄求者。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "To have remonstrance officials speak thus is very good; it can stop reckless petitioners in days to come."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said: "To have remonstrance officials speak thus is very good. It can stop reckless petitioners in days to come."

sentences.zh: 以密州觀察使卒，賜昭德軍節度使，諡曰惠節。

translations.literal: He died as Inspector of Mi Prefecture; he was granted Military Governor of Zhaode Army and given the posthumous title Huijie.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as inspector of Mi Prefecture. He was granted military governor of Zhaode Army and given the posthumous title Huijie.

sentences.zh: 傳範，宰相子，聯戚裏，所至有能稱。

translations.literal: Chuanfan was the son of a chief minister and linked by imperial kinship; wherever he went he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanfan was the son of a chief minister and linked by imperial kinship. Wherever he went he earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 以橐中貲千餘萬葬族人在殯者六十四喪。

translations.literal: With more than ten million in his purse he buried sixty-four clansmen whose coffins had been awaiting interment.
translations.idiomatic: With more than ten million in his purse he buried sixty-four clansmen whose coffins had been awaiting interment.

sentences.zh: 從侄經、綜。

translations.literal: His cousins were Jing and Zong.
translations.idiomatic: His cousins were Jing and Zong.

sentences.zh: 經字審禮，以蔭至虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Shenli, through hereditary privilege rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, courtesy name Shenli, through hereditary privilege rose to outer gentleman of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 神宗為穎王，選經女為妃，改莊宅使。

translations.literal: When Shenzong was Prince of Ying, he selected Jing's daughter as consort; Jing was changed to Director of the Estates Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong was Prince of Ying, he selected Jing's daughter as consort, and Jing was changed to director of the Estates Office.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，妃為皇后，進光州團練使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, the consort became empress, and Jing was promoted to Regimental Commander of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor ascended the throne, the consort became empress, and Jing was promoted to regimental commander of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以濰州防禦使知陳州，歲中閱囚，活重辟三人。

translations.literal: As Defender of Wei Prefecture he commanded Chen Prefecture; midyear he reviewed prisoners and spared three men facing capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: As defender of Wei Prefecture he commanded Chen Prefecture. Midyear he reviewed prisoners and spared three men facing capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 西華令掠人至死，誣以疾，吏畏令，莫敢言。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xihua abducted a man until he died and falsely claimed it was illness; the clerks feared the magistrate and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Xihua abducted a man until he died and falsely claimed it was illness. The clerks feared the magistrate and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 經得其情，卒窮治如法。

translations.literal: Jing got to the truth of the matter and in the end pursued the case to the full extent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Jing got to the truth of the matter and in the end pursued the case to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 歲大雪，輒弛公私僦錢以寬民，有司持不 可，經曰：「上使我守陳，民窮蓋我責，我自為此，不爾累也。」

translations.literal: In a year of heavy snow he repeatedly waived public and private rental payments to relieve the people; the officials held this impermissible; Jing said: "The sovereign sent me to guard Chen — if the people are destitute it is my responsibility; I do this myself and will not involve you."
translations.idiomatic: In a year of heavy snow he repeatedly waived public and private rental payments to relieve the people. The officials held this impermissible. Jing said: "The sovereign sent me to guard Chen. If the people are destitute it is my responsibility. I do this myself and will not involve you."

sentences.zh: 方鎮別賜公使錢，例私以自奉，去則盡入其餘，經獨斥歸有司，唯以供享勞賓客軍師之用。

translations.literal: Military governors were separately granted public envoy funds, which by custom they kept for personal use and upon leaving deposited the remainder entirely for themselves; Jing alone returned them to the officials, using them only for sacrifices, entertaining guests, and rewarding military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors were separately granted public envoy funds, which by custom they kept for personal use and upon leaving kept the remainder for themselves. Jing alone returned them to the officials, using them only for sacrifices, entertaining guests, and rewarding military officers.

sentences.zh: 知河 陽，會旱蝗，民乏食，經度官廩歲用無餘，乃先以圭田租入振救之，富人爭出粟，多所濟活。

translations.literal: He commanded Heyang; drought and locusts struck, and the people lacked food. Jing calculated that the official granaries had nothing left for the year's use, so he first used the rent from the fief fields for relief; the wealthy competed to offer grain, and many were saved.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Heyang when drought and locusts struck and the people lacked food. Jing calculated that the official granaries had nothing left for the year's use, so he first used rent from the fief fields for relief. The wealthy competed to offer grain, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 徙徐州，遷明州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xu Prefecture and promoted to Inspector of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xu Prefecture and promoted to inspector of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召還，提舉景靈宮。

translations.literal: He was recalled and put in charge of Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and put in charge of Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 進定國軍留 後，復出知青州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Military Governor of Dingguo Army and again went out to command Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting military governor of Dingguo Army and again went out to command Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既行，官給車徒，三宮皆遣使送之，車馬相屬於道。

translations.literal: After he set out, the court provided carriage and escort; all three palaces sent envoys to see him off, and carriages and horses stretched in succession along the road.
translations.idiomatic: After he set out, the court provided carriage and escort. All three palaces sent envoys to see him off, and carriages and horses stretched in succession along the road.

sentences.zh: 未逾歲，得疾還，卒於淄州，年五十四。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed he fell ill and returned; he died at Zi Prefecture at the age of fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed he fell ill and returned. He died at Zi Prefecture at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 詔內侍迎其喪，皇后出哭於新昌第。

translations.literal: An edict ordered palace attendants to meet his coffin; the empress came out to weep at his Xinchang residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered palace attendants to meet his coffin. The empress came out to weep at his Xinchang residence.

sentences.zh: 喪至，慶壽、寶 慈宮交遣謁者予叕，後臨於國門之外。

translations.literal: When the coffin arrived, Shouqing and Baochi Palaces alternately sent ushers to receive it; the empress attended outside the Gate of the Nation.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin arrived, Shouqing and Baochi Palaces alternately sent ushers to receive it. The empress attended outside the Gate of the Nation.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，諡曰康懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Secretariat Director and given the posthumous title Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Secretariat director and given the posthumous title Kangyi.

sentences.zh: 將葬，遣近臣典護穿復土，給太常鹵簿。

translations.literal: When he was about to be buried, close ministers were dispatched to oversee the excavation and reburial, and the Grand Music Office procession was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be buried, close ministers were dispatched to oversee the excavation and reburial, and the Grand Music Office procession was granted.

sentences.zh: 帝出郊奠之，周視其柩。

translations.literal: The Emperor went out to the suburbs to offer sacrifice and walked around viewing the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went out to the suburbs to offer sacrifice and walked around viewing the coffin.

sentences.zh: 葬三日，後臨於墓下，賜篆碑首曰「忠 勤懿戚」。

translations.literal: Three days after the burial the empress attended below the tomb and granted the seal-script inscription for the stele head: "Loyal, Diligent, and Worthy Kinsman."
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the burial the empress attended below the tomb and granted the seal-script inscription for the stele head: "Loyal, Diligent, and Worthy Kinsman."

sentences.zh: 經所至勤吏治，事皆自省決，頗欲以才見於用，故數請外補。

translations.literal: Wherever Jing went he diligently administered officials; he decided matters himself and very much wished to be employed for his talent, and so repeatedly requested outside appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Jing went he diligently administered officials and decided matters himself. He very much wished to be employed for his talent and so repeatedly requested outside appointments.

sentences.zh: 嘗因太祖忌日，百官班開元殿下，後召經見行幄，勉以盡忠朝廷，經亦以善事三宮為言，不及其家事。

translations.literal: Once on Taizu's death anniversary the hundred officials lined up below Kaiyuan Hall; the empress summoned Jing to her traveling pavilion and urged him to serve the court with full loyalty; Jing also spoke of serving the three palaces well and did not mention his family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once on Taizu's death anniversary the hundred officials lined up below Kaiyuan Hall. The empress summoned Jing to her traveling pavilion and urged him to serve the court with full loyalty. Jing also spoke of serving the three palaces well and did not mention his family affairs.

sentences.zh: 子宗回、宗良。

translations.literal: His sons were Zonghui and Zongliang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zonghui and Zongliang.

sentences.zh: 綜字君章，知歙縣，籍閭里惡少年，有盜發，用以推跡輒得。

translations.literal: Zong, courtesy name Junzhang, commanded She County; he registered the bad youths of the neighborhoods, and when a theft occurred he used them to track it down and always succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, courtesy name Junzhang, commanded She County. He registered the bad youths of the neighborhoods, and when a theft occurred he used them to track it down and always succeeded.

sentences.zh: 通判桂州、常州，知隨、鼎、漳、汾、密、棣、沂七州。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Gui and Chang Prefectures and commanded the seven prefectures of Sui, Ding, Zhang, Fen, Mi, Di, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Gui and Chang Prefectures and commanded the seven prefectures of Sui, Ding, Zhang, Fen, Mi, Di, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 沂阻山多盜，綜請用重法繩禁，歲斷大辟減 半。

translations.literal: Yi was blocked by mountains and had many bandits; Zong requested strict laws to restrain them, and capital cases in a year were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was blocked by mountains and had many bandits. Zong requested strict laws to restrain them, and capital cases in a year were reduced by half.

sentences.zh: 兵久惰，會初置官提舉，教之急，眾不悅，監兵夜排闥告變，綜疑有他謀，就寢自若。

translations.literal: The troops had long been slack; when officials were first appointed to supervise them and training was urgently imposed, the men were displeased; the supervising soldiers burst through the door at night to report a mutiny; Zong suspected another plot and went to sleep as usual.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had long been slack. When officials were first appointed to supervise them and training was urgently imposed, the men were displeased. The supervising soldiers burst through the door at night to report a mutiny. Zong suspected another plot and went to sleep as usual.

sentences.zh: 明日大閱，申嚴號令，賞其高強，罰其不進者，卒亦無事。

translations.literal: The next day he held a grand review, strictly enforced commands, rewarded the strong performers and punished those who did not advance, and in the end nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he held a grand review, strictly enforced commands, rewarded the strong performers and punished those who did not advance, and in the end nothing happened.

sentences.zh: 性寬裕，善治 劇，於奸惡不少恕。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous, skilled at handling difficult cases, and showed little mercy to the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was generous and skilled at handling difficult cases, yet showed little mercy to the wicked.

sentences.zh: 官累中散大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He successively reached Grand Master of Palace Attendance and died.
translations.idiomatic: He successively reached grand master of palace attendance and died.

sentences.zh: 宗回字子發，累官相州觀察使。

translations.literal: Zonghui, courtesy name Zifa, successively reached Inspector of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui, courtesy name Zifa, successively reached inspector of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，進彰德軍留後。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Acting Military Governor of Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong ascended the throne, he was promoted to acting military governor of Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 曆安國、保信、鎮南、保平軍節度使，檢校司空，封 永陽、寧海、安康、漢東郡王，開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He successively served as Military Governor of Anguo, Baoxin, Zhennan, and Baoping Armies, was made Honorary Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Yongyang, Ninghai, Ankang, and Handong Commanderies, and granted Grand Master with the same ceremony as the Three Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as military governor of Anguo, Baoxin, Zhennan, and Baoping Armies, was made honorary minister of works, enfeoffed as duke of Yongyang, Ninghai, Ankang, and Handong Commanderies, and granted grand master with ceremonial standing equal to the Three Councillors.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，有告其陰事者，詔開封府鞫實，御史中丞吳執中臨問，宗回惶懼，上還印綬，以太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning someone reported his secret affairs; an edict ordered Kaifeng Prefecture to investigate; Censor-in-Chief Wu Zhizhong personally questioned him; Zonghui was fearful and returned his seal and credentials, retiring as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongning someone reported his secret affairs. An edict ordered Kaifeng Prefecture to investigate, and censor-in-chief Wu Zhizhong personally questioned him. Zonghui was fearful and returned his seal and credentials, retiring as junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 言者不已， 削官爵流郴州。

translations.literal: The accusers did not stop; his rank and titles were stripped and he was exiled to Chen Prefecture.
